generated_by: scripts/nfl_questions.py (curated register, each row tied to a source or a blank)
how_to_read: status=answered: the answer is published and every value it depends on is source-linked.
status=partial: some part is answered and the rest is a named gap.
status=open: cannot be answered with the information the project holds today.
blocking=yes means no bet/strategy/decision of that class should proceed until it is answered.
Every open/partial row names the exact evidence that would close it and who owns it.

questions.question: May this project legally store, derive from and publish NFL-derived statistics and lines?
questions.have: NFL.com Terms updated 2024-05-16 section 1.3 permits use of NFL.com Services 'solely for your own individual non-commercial and informational purposes' and prohibits systematic retrieval to compile a database without written consent. NFL.com is a Service, so that clause governs reading it; it is quoted on the Sources page.
questions.missing: Written consent from NFL Enterprises for any systematic collection, and a licence review for the community data used for the backtest (no license file found).
questions.would_close: A signed licence or written permission; or a switch to a licensed data provider with an auditable contract.

questions.question: Is the community game log (leesharpe/nfldata) licensed for redistribution of derived values?
questions.have: Repository metadata shows no licence file at retrieval (2026-11-12); a second community source (nflverse-data) is CC-BY-4.0.
questions.missing: An explicit licence statement from the repository owner.
questions.would_close: Licence file or written permission; otherwise replace with nflverse-data (CC-BY-4.0) once it is downloadable in the build environment.

questions.question: What are the current, executable lines for the Week 10 slate?
questions.have: Nothing. No official NFL line feed exists; sportsbook prices are contractual and were not fetched. Every market cell on the Own Lines page is blank by rule.
questions.missing: A timestamped, licensed price archive (open, close, and the exact book) for each selection.
questions.would_close: A data contract with a book/aggregator plus a hash-stamped capture job.

questions.question: Do the historical closing lines in the community file match any real book?
questions.have: Only that the file reports one closing spread/total per game, with no book, timestamp, or vig.
questions.missing: Book identity and capture time; the -110 price assumption used in the backtest is labelled as an assumption.
questions.would_close: A source that names the book and the capture timestamp for each closing line.

questions.question: Does the ratings model beat the closing line on a season it never saw?
questions.have: 2025 holdout (fit 2015-2024): S1 spread bets n=172, ROI -1.2% [-12.3%, +10.4%]; S2 totals n=111, ROI -3.7% [-24.3%, +17.3%]; S3 moneylines n=219, ROI -7.5% [-28.0%, +15.3%]. No interval excludes zero; the only significant effect is negative.
questions.missing: A season where the lower bound clears zero after paying vig, which the current signal family does not produce.
questions.would_close: A validated signal (gate G05-G10 all pass) on a new holdout season.

questions.question: How large must the sample be before a real edge could be detected?
questions.have: The gate floor of 200 bets / 200 games / 60 slate dates, plus the bootstrap width actually observed (about +/-11 points of ROI at n=172).
questions.missing: Nothing; the answer is a design property.

questions.question: Are 'home cover' and 'over' independent on the same game?
questions.have: 2,792 games 2015-2025: phi=+0.022 [-0.010, +0.056] clustered, Fisher [-0.015, +0.059], Fisher exact p=0.24. Observed joint 24.39% vs 23.83% if independent (ratio 1.023). Independence is not rejected, but the point estimate is positive.
questions.missing: A season of same-game player-prop outcomes to test real prop combos, which is where dependence is usually large.
questions.would_close: Licensed player-level prop history paired by game.

questions.question: What is the dependence structure of player-prop combos (QB yards + WR yards, etc.)?
questions.have: Nothing. No prop history and no prop lines were obtained.
questions.missing: Player-level outcomes per game and prop thresholds with prices.
questions.would_close: A licensed prop feed plus paired residual construction on training seasons only.

questions.question: Which Week 10 starters are confirmed out or limited, and who is the published backup?
questions.have: 275 injury rows transcribed from the official Week 10 report; only 6 carry an explicit game status (Out/Questionable). Depth charts read for WAS, NYG, DET: 13 starter-level deficiencies computed with published weights.

questions.question: How many points is a starter injury worth to the line?
questions.have: A transparent index (position weight x string gap x status risk) with a 3.0 points-per-index assumption. It is an assumption, not an estimate.
questions.missing: A timestamped historical injury archive with pre/post lines, to regress line movement on the index.

questions.have: Frozen gates G01-G10 (rights, provenance, chronology, sample floor, calibration, ROI lower bound, CLV lower bound, Bonferroni family, dependence sample, deflated Sharpe). Ranking uses only the lower bound. Rewards are non-monetary research priority.

questions.have: A reward ladder exists in code (Tier A/B/C research priority), but nobody has ever passed.
